data.content_ref: inline:{"analogy":null,"claim":"There are 648 valid three-digit numbers with all distinct digits, derived by removing the 288 numbers with at least one repeated digit from the 900 total.","counterconditions":[{"case":"If the complement count 288 is asserted without correcting for over-subtraction of AAA forms, the math is inconsistent.","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"},{"case":"If the inclusion-exclusion correction is misapplied (e.g., adding back 9 instead of 18), the result diverges from 648.","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"},{"case":"If the alphabet for the complement calculation does not restrict the hundreds digit to 1-9, the categories AAB, ABA, BAA will have incorrect sizes.","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"}],"definitions":[],"derivation":[],"formalization_refs":[],"mechanism":"Start with 900 total three-digit numbers. Count the complement: numbers with at least one repeated digit. These have the form AAB (81: 9 hundreds \u00d7 1 match \u00d7 9 free), ABA (81), or BAA (72: 9 hundreds \u00d7 8 non-matching tens \u00d7 1 match). Sum = 81 + 81 + 72 = 234. However, AAA (9) is subtracted three times in this sum, so add back 2 \u00d7 9 = 18. Total repeats = 234 + 18 = 252. Valid numbers = 900 - 252 = 648.","premises":[],"schema":"deepreason-reasoning-envelope-v1","scope":{"covers":[],"excludes":[]},"simulation_refs":[],"uncertainties":[]}
